capitals.name: Lakhiarviro
capitals.note: Infobox Capitals: Lakhiarviro (1147-1548); Bhuj (1549-1947). The page does not place Lakhiarviro; the centre of the Eastern Cutch shape stands in for it.

capitals.name: Bhuj
capitals.note: Khengarji "shifted his capital to Bhuj"; the infobox gives 1549-1947 and the text has Lakhiarviro ending in 1548.

rulers.name: Lakho Jadani
rulers.note: Table; "ruled Eastern Cutch from 1147 to 1175". The page gives Rao Hamirji 1472-1536 and Jam Raval 1540-1548 for the line before Khengarji.

rulers.name: Khengarji I
rulers.note: "formally ascended throne at Rapar in year 1534"; "integrated Cutch into one large dominion in 1549"; founder of Cutch State on the page.

rulers.name: Fateh Muhammad
rulers.note: Regent 1801-1813; the page also says the council "made Fateh Muhammad ruler ... who ably ruled Cutch from 1786 to 1813".

rulers.name: Vijayaraji
rulers.note: Died 26 January 1948 (the text: 26 February 1948 on the Kutch State page).

rulers.name: Madansinhji
rulers.note: Last ruler, signed the Instrument of Accession on 16 August 1947 on behalf of his father.

The page says Lakho Jadani "ruled Eastern Cutch from 1147 to 1175" and that Khengarji I "integrated Cutch into one large dominion in 1549"; the extent before 1549 is not given, so the part of the Kutch mainland east of about 70.2 E (about 3,800 km2, Wagad and Rapar, where Khengarji ascended in 1534) stands in for all of 1147-1548. ledger.counterpart: Chawda and Chaulukya dynasties (the page's predecessors)
ledger.note: About 1147: Lakho Jadani founds the Kingdom of Kutch. "A predecessor state known as the Kingdom of Kutch was founded around 1147 by Lakho Jadani" (infobox Established: 1147); he ruled "Eastern Cutch from 1147 to 1175". The Jadejas "migrated from Sindh in the late 12th century". The Jadeja page dates the dynasty differently (oral sources the late 9th century, written sources the 14th, and "ruled the princely state of Kutch from 1540"); the dossier follows the Cutch State infobox.
1549: the capital moves from Lakhiarviro to Bhuj. Infobox Capitals: "Lakhiarviro (1147-1548); Bhuj (1549-1947)"; Khengarji I "shifted his capital to Bhuj".

ledger.counterpart: Jadeja chieftains of Cutch (Jam Raval and others)
ledger.note: 1549: Khengarji I unifies Cutch. He "integrated Cutch into one large dominion in 1549" after "formally ascend[ing] throne at Rapar in year 1534"; the table has Jam Raval 1540-1548 before Khengarji I 1548-1585. The page names no rival or boundary: the counterpart and the west of Kutch (everything but Eastern Cutch) are my reading.

25 December 1815: Anjar comes under British occupation. "On 15 December 1815, the army of Cutch state was defeated near Bhadreswar, Kutch," by combined British and Gaekwad forces; Anjar "came under British occupation on 25 December 1815".
25 December 1822: Anjar reverts to Cutch. Anjar remained under occupation "till 25 December 1822, when it was territory reverted to Cutch by an agreement".

ledger.note: 1 June 1948: Cutch is placed under the Government of India. "On 1 June 1948 the administration was transferred to the Government of India, working through a Chief Commissioner"; Cutch State infobox "Merged into India as Kutch State: 1 June 1948", while its text says the administration was merged "till 4 May 1948, when the administration of the state was completely merged". The ruler Madansinhji signed the Instrument of Accession on 16 August 1947 (Cutch State page). The Kutch State (1948-1956) continued as a Class C state from 26 January 1950 until 1 November 1956.

wars.outcome: Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhoro of Sindh "attacked Cutch twice once in 1763-64" and "again in 1765"; the page gives no result, and in 1770 a daughter of Wesuji was married to the Mian Kalhoro.
wars.note: The kalhora-dynasty dossier is in this batch.

wars.name: Anglo-Gaekwad campaign against Kutch
wars.outcome: On 15 December 1815 the army of Cutch was defeated near Bhadreswar by combined British and Gaekwad forces; Anjar was occupied by the British from 25 December 1815 to 25 December 1822, when it reverted to Cutch by agreement; the Jadeja rulers accepted British suzerainty in 1819.
wars.note: The page does not name an Anglo-Kutch war or a treaty of 1816; the 1785 revolt of Meghji Seth of Anjar and the 1819 earthquake (famines 1823, 1825, 1832) are on the page without territorial result.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; Eastern Cutch is a reading of "ruled Eastern Cutch".
The page gives 19,725 km2 (1901) and no boundary; the shape is the Kutch mainland polygon.

sources.title: Cutch State
sources.note: Kingdom of Kutch founded about 1147 by Lakho Jadani; Khengarji I integrated Cutch in 1549 and Bhuj capital 1549; 1719 Mughal invasion; Kalhora attacks 1763-65; 1785 revolt; 15 December 1815 defeat near Bhadreswar and Anjar occupation 25 December 1815 to 25 December 1822; British suzerainty 1819; accession 16 August 1947; merger 1 June 1948 (4 May 1948 in the text); area 19,725 km2 (1901).

sources.title: Kutch State
sources.note: The state after 1948: administration transferred to the Government of India on 1 June 1948 through a Chief Commissioner; Class C state 26 January 1950; Bombay State 1 November 1956; Gujarat 1 May 1960; silent on area, founding and capital.

sources.title: Jadeja
sources.note: Jadeja dynasty of Kutch from 1540 to 1948 (page); Khengar raised to Rao and granted Morvi in 1538 by the Sultan of Gujarat; oral and written dates for the Jadejas conflict; silent on the extent of Kutch, Bhuj and 1549.

notes: Three pages opened (Cutch State, Kutch State, Jadeja). The first fetch of Kutch State described the post-1948 state and is silent on founding, capital, area and the Jadejas; Cutch State is the page of the princely state and is the source of the identity and territory. The Jadeja page is cited only for the dynasty dates, which conflict with the Cutch State infobox. Conflicts: end 1 June 1948 (infobox) against 4 May 1948 (text); Khengarji I ascended at Rapar in 1534 and unified Cutch in 1549 (the Jadeja page has the 1538 grant of Morvi); Vijayaraji died 26 January 1948 (Cutch State) or 26 February 1948 (Kutch State). Natural Earth and the gazetteer region Kutch include the Great Rann and measure 62,000 km2, three times the page area, so a polygon cut to India is used. british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start for cutch-state from 1819 (the page: "accepted the suzerainty of British in 1819") to 1947; kalhora-dynasty and baroda-state are the counterparts of the wars. The anjar occupation has no pair in the british-empire dossier. Counterparts needing dossiers: chaulukya-dynasty (if it has no row), kutch-state 1948-1956 (the Class C state; post-independence).
